title: Chapter 9: Weathering, Mass Wasting and Erosion

blocks.content: Weathering is an in-situ or on-site process, where little or no motion of materials takes place from one place to another.

items: Crucial distinction: Weathering is purely an in-situ (static) process, whereas Erosion is an ex-situ (dynamic) process involving transport.
Categorize mass movements accurately: Soil creep and solifluction are extremely slow, while rockfalls, mudflows, and debris avalanches are rapid.
Exfoliation domes and tors result primarily from unloading, pressure release, and thermal expansion in crystalline rocks like granite.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Weathering is an in-situ or static process involving the mechanical disintegration and chemical decomposition of rocks without significant transportation.
Mass wasting refers to the downslope movement of rock debris, soil, and regolith primarily under the direct influence of gravity.
Physical weathering processes rely on thermal expansion, frost action, and unloading, dominant in dry or high-altitude environments.
Chemical weathering includes hydration, carbonation, oxidation, and solution, operating most rapidly in warm and humid climates.
Erosion is an active, dynamic exogenic process that involves the acquisition and transportation of rock materials by mobile agents such as water, wind, glaciers, and waves.
